image_prompt: A stern unmarried woman in her late fifties to early sixties, gaunt and thin-framed with sharp, angular facial features that speak to years of bitterness and isolation. Her face is deeply lined with vertical creases around her tight, pursed mouth and horizontal furrows across her forehead. Pale, sallow complexion characteristic of Northern European winters and indoor confinement. Steel-gray hair pulled severely back into a tight bun covered by a plain white linen cap typical of 1720s German spinster dress. She wears a high-necked, austere black woolen dress with long sleeves and no ornamentation, reflecting Lutheran simplicity and mourning customs. A simple white collar at the neck, starched and rigid. Her eyes are narrow, calculating, and slightly sunken with dark circles beneath them. Thin, bloodless lips pressed into a disapproving expression. Bony, work-worn hands with prominent knuckles clasped together. Her posture is rigid and upright, conveying moral severity and suppressed resentment. The overall appearance suggests a woman hardened by spinsterhood in a harsh provincial setting.
book_context: Historical biography of Catherine the Great (Sophie Friederike Auguste von Anhalt-Zerbst)
